name: Improved Kilo-class submarine (Project 636.3)

placement_rationale.text: 440 km, slightly closer to zero than the surface-fleet frigate entry (480 km) but still deep strategic_rear, matches this asset's own contrast_vs_traditional: submerged and 'effectively immune' to the USV threat that forced Black Sea Fleet surface units out of Sevastopol, so it does not need to stand off as far as a surface combatant to stay survivable, while basing from the same relocated Black Sea Fleet posture (4th Independent Submarine Brigade) that doctrine.md §2's air/sea-superiority finding predicts for any asset in a contested maritime domain. USNI Proceedings and Naval News (both already in sources) document continued Kalibr firings from submerged positions in the Black Sea throughout the war even after the surface fleet's relocation, consistent with a deep-rear but slightly-forward-of-the-surface-fleet placement.

sources.label: USNI Proceedings — Russia's Kilo-class Submarine: Improved And More Deadly Than Ever
Naval News — Russia's improved Kilo-class submarine entering Black Sea

cost.display: ~$300-350M per hull (derived from a six-boat export contract; Russia's own internal procurement cost is not publicly disclosed)

key_facts.label: Armament
key_facts.value: 6x 21-inch torpedo tubes; Kalibr land-attack/anti-ship cruise missiles fired through the tubes

key_facts.label: Unit
key_facts.value: 4th Independent Submarine Brigade, Black Sea Fleet

short_role: Diesel-electric attack submarine, land-attack cruise missile launch platform
characteristics: 6x 21-inch bow torpedo tubes; up to 18 torpedoes or 24 mines, or Kalibr cruise missiles fired from the tubes
Extremely quiet for its class — Western navies nicknamed the original Kilo the "Black Hole"
Strength: submerged, effectively immune to the USV attacks that have driven the Black Sea Fleet's surface units out of Sevastopol
Limitation: diesel-electric, not nuclear — must snorkel/surface periodically to recharge batteries, the one window it's vulnerable in
Estimated quantity available: 6 boats assigned to the Black Sea Fleet's submarine brigade
employment_notes: Has continued firing Kalibr land-attack cruise missiles at Ukraine from submerged positions in the Black Sea throughout the war, even after the surface fleet's relocation from Sevastopol to Novorossiysk — submersion is what keeps it employable in a sea Ukraine's USVs and anti-ship missiles have made increasingly costly for surface combatants to operate in.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional naval doctrine treated a battle fleet's most valuable strike asset as its surface combatants, with submarines in a supporting anti-ship/reconnaissance role. Ukraine's USV campaign has inverted that locally in the Black Sea: a submerged submarine is now the more survivable land-attack missile platform of the two, precisely because it doesn't have to sit at a pier or transit open water where a $250k drone boat can reach it.
